text:
Tim Washe has 50 hits and 25 blocked shots in 17 games, the line of a player doing the hard jobs for a Ducks team on a four-game winning streak. He's 25, undrafted out of Western Michigan, and this is his first full NHL season after 41 games before it.

He's chipped in 6 points, with 3 goals on 2.28 expected, and his shooting is running hot. The on-ice numbers are tough: Anaheim takes 40% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him at five on five, almost six points worse than without him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking puts it plainly: his game isn't built on creating offense, so his value has to come elsewhere.

That's the penalty kill and the matchup work, and the Ducks clearly trust him: 15 minutes a night, and 20:36 in the overtime loss to Vancouver. His speed is good (84th percentile top speed), which helps on the forecheck. We project about 13 goals. For an undrafted forward who had 12 points in his last college season, sticking in the lineup of a winning team is the story.
headline: Tim Washe's heavy minutes
